sentences.text: 1  CONSTITUTION OF INDIA PRAYING TO QUASH THE NOTIFICATION  DATED 12.7.2017 BY RESPONDENTS VIDE ANNEX-A AND ETC.,

THIS WP, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT  MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2023:KHC:32404  WP No. 38718 of 2018  ORDER 1.

The petitioner is before this Court seeking for the following reliefs:
a. Issue a writ in the nature of certiorari and quash the notification bearing No.
BBMP/RAV/TDR/04/2017-18 dated 12.07.2017 by respondents vide Annexure-A, b.
Declare that the respondents cannot compel the petitioner to forego his land and buildings/schedule property by accepting the Transferable Development Rights in lieu of monetary compensation, c. Direct the respondents to record the dissent of the petitioner for accepting transferable Development Rights and direct them to apply the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act of 2013 in relation to payment of monetary compensation.
d. Grant costs, e. Grant such other relief or reliefs as this Hon'ble Court may deem fit in the circumstances of the case.
2. The petitioner is the owner of land covered under Sy.No.45/2.

The respondents, by way of a notification dated 12.07.2017 have initiated a proposal to acquire the lands for widening of the existing road from Ibbalur Junction to Chickkanahalli Road Railway Over Bridge, Sarjapura Main Road, Bengaluru, by invoking Section 14(B) of the Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961 (for short 'KTCP Act').

entities.text: Karnataka Town and Country Planning Act, 1961
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The respondents having offered transferable development rights to the petitioner, the petitioner is not willing to accept the same and has insisted on compensation in money terms to be paid as NC: 2023:KHC:32404 regards the said acquisition, which is made in terms of the demarcation of the widening of the road under Section 12 of the KTCP Act read with Section 69 of the KTCP Act since the respondents were not willing to make payment of compensation in terms of money.
In that background, the petitioner is before this court seeking for the aforesaid reliefs.

3. Counsel for the petitioner relies upon a decision of the Coordinate Bench of this court dated 03.04.2019 in W.P.No.16816/2018 to contend that the acquisition by issuance of transferable development rights is only an option which can be made available by the acquiring authority, there can be no compulsion on part of the petitioner, it is for the land loser, to accept the transferable development rights who can also insist upon compensation in terms of money.

2 4.

entities.text: Sri K N Mohan vs Bruhat Bangalore Mahanagara Palike
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A perusal of the said decision supports the submission made by the counsel for the petitioner.

A reading of Section 69 of the KTCP Act indicates that if the municipal authority in order to implement the reservation made in NC: 2023:KHC:32404 the Revised Master Plan for widening of any road, then the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 are required to be invoked.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
In that view of the matter, when the petitioner is not ready to accept transferable development rights, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.
(ii) A certiorari is issued, the notification bearing No.BBMP/RAV/TDR/04/2017-18 dated 12.07.2017 at Annexure-A is quashed.

Liberty is reserved to the respondents to initiate acquisition proceedings in terms of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
Sd/-
